notes: Decomposition spec for the atomization migration. Descriptive lane (complete coverage required): 'aggregate' retypes a conjunctive attestation to aggregation in place (id and claim unchanged), minting the listed atoms as attestations that carry the parent's artifact/kind/domain/tags/subjects, with the parent's deps set to the atom ids; 'trim' rewrites a claim to its conclusion (deps carry the basis); 'keep' passes through with a recorded reason. Prescriptive lane (incremental; absent prescriptions pass through): 'restate' rewrites the claim to the norm, moves enumerable normative content to invariants, and optionally extracts descriptive rationale to atoms (atom_kind, atom_artifact) appended to deps. Atom ids are generator-assigned: aggregates ascending then restates ascending, sequential from id_base, so descriptive atom ids stay stable as prescriptive entries accrete.

atoms: Compound assertions survive session boundaries - an implication created in March is still there in April, still linked to its deps, still flaggable if a dep changes.
Without the DAG, every session re-reads raw data and reconstructs some fraction of the reasoning, losing compound insights that depend on having the right facts adjacent at the right time.
Sources are not beliefs: a source document is raw material from which primitives are extracted.
The graph stores structured beliefs; sources store evidence.
The source-belief relationship is bidirectional - sources feed primitives upstream and syntheses reference belief IDs downstream - and both directions can be active on the same document.
Multi-paragraph analyses should not be belief kinds.
The schema is built around atomic, composable beliefs - the claim field is a one-liner.
Stuffing prose into a belief inverts the relationship: the prose becomes the point and the claim becomes a title.
Analyses live as source documents referencing belief IDs inline.
Self-referential beliefs use the existing schema with subject type 'agent' - no special case needed.
Self-referential beliefs capture agent operational patterns, failure modes, and collaboration dynamics using the same primitive/compound/implication structure as domain beliefs.
Human-observed data (corrections, failure observations) produces the highest-quality self-referential primitives.
A traversal-path belief presents a path through graph nodes rather than synthesizing deps into a single belief - the routing IS the argument.
A traversal-path's conclusion is separable from its routing, enabling independent evaluation.
Field-level provenance (_provenance block on entities) maps source documents to the specific fields they substantiate.
Field-level provenance makes the data model 100% auditable - if the agent tells you something, you can check the source.
Under field-level provenance, errors become real-time hallucinations, not deep data mistakes.

cb:b131.note: Inference; claim enumerates its basis but the conclusion (retroactive attribution prohibited at every layer) is one claim. Candidate for a later trim pass.

atoms: Contracts fill the abstraction gap between literal code and plain English for supervising agentic coding.

The system had implicit contracts scattered across three representations: structs (shape without behavioral invariants), skills (workflow without guarantees to callers), and the agent-instruction file (policy without mechanical verification).
Contracts make implicit guarantees explicit, machine-readable, and verifiable.
Contracts are bound to domain, not implementation - they survive code rewrites.
A domain expert can author contracts without understanding code; a coding agent can implement against them without understanding business context.
Contracts generate tests, not the other way around: if you rewrote a module from scratch, every test breaks but the contract stays the same.
Contracts govern behavior across fundamentally different substrates.
A single state-machine contract was independently implemented in compiled code and in agent reasoning, producing identical results without either knowing about the other.
A contract serves as intermediary: a domain expert authors it, an architect verifies against it, implementations derive from it.

cb:b138.claim: Contracts constitute the abstraction layer between domain expertise and implementation.
cb:b138.note: Claim previously restated its three deps (b133, b134, b135) as a numbered basis; per claim-discipline (b402) the deps carry the basis and the claim carries the conclusion.

cb:b173.claim: Implications are prototypes for contracts: an implication encodes a behavioral invariant at the prompt level, and when code crystallizes around that invariant the implication is elevated to a contract, while implications that can never become contracts (pure reasoning directives, tone guidance) stay implications indefinitely.
cb:b173.note: Compressed from six sentences to the conclusion; the enforcement-boundary basis lives in dep b174.

atoms: Implications are behavioral directives - they shape how the agent reasons and acts.
Implications work through the prompt (surfaced via _patches.md) and are 'soft': compliance depends on the agent reading and following them.
Implications are durable - they survive session boundaries and compose with deps that explain why the rule exists.
Contracts are structural invariants - they are verified by code (verify_against_contract/0).

A contract such as 'loan status transitions must follow this state machine' is testable because the Elixir module hardcodes the transitions and the test compares them to the DAG definition - if code drifts from the contract, the test fails, a strict guarantee.
The implication-contract boundary is the enforcement mechanism: implications are enforced by the prompt, contracts are enforced by code.

cb:b339.note: Second sentence operationalizes the first, not a separable assertion; the node was itself already decomposed from a coarser claim.

atoms: When a writable field carries a user-authored provenance entry (user: or manual:) and a subsequent sync pass ingests an artifact that disagrees, a pure overlay policy (user-wins) silently hides the contradiction.
When a writable field carries a user-authored provenance entry and a subsequent sync pass ingests an artifact that disagrees, a pure artifact-wins policy silently discards the user edit.
Both user-vs-artifact divergence failure modes are invisible without explicit conflict detection at write time.

cb:b376.note: Conjunctive, but the node carries no artifact, so decomposition would mint ungrounded atoms; deferred to an evidence-repair pass.

atoms: Implication lifecycle field `status` (active | superseded | retracted, per b029) describes whether the claim is still true.
Implication lifecycle field `materialized` (null | {plan, date}) describes whether the action was executed; status and materialized are orthogonal.
An active-and-unmaterialized implication is still-actionable work; an active-and-materialized implication has been discharged at time T and remains true as a principle.
The two-field lifecycle preserves b029's closed status enum while giving discrete implications a first-class discharged state via `materialized`, which a363 and downstream implications already use.
a373's proposal of `materialized` as a fifth status value was authored without preflight DAG search and therefore without consensus, and is superseded by the two-field design.
The `materialized` field records a historical fact - the action was executed at time T via plan P - and does not assert that the action's effects still hold.
Materialization effects decay: code drifts, principles stop being enforced, refactors regress.

The `materialized` field carries a `last_verified` sub-field distinguishing historical execution from current verification, with shape `materialized: null | {plan: path, date: ISO, last_verified: null | ISO}`.
A fresh materialization has `last_verified: null`; an audited-and-still-current materialization has `last_verified` set to the audit date.
Drift detection for materialized effects is handled by a separate audit cycle.

A digest file caching active implications, regenerated by command, has freshness that depends on procedural enforcement - agents can and do forget, producing a stale digest read as authoritative by subsequent sessions.
Persisted caches of graph-derived content whose freshness is procedural rather than structural are antipatterns; they embed the staleness risk they were meant to solve.
The elimination path for the digest antipattern: fold active-implication loading into a session-start belief query and render the digest live from the graph instead of from disk.
Deprecation is a pause, not a retirement: the decision is 'not currently useful enough to carry' rather than 'wrong forever'.
The deprecation primitive records the reasoning for why the feature failed to earn its keep.
A deprecated feature can be reinstated under new adjudication: the supersession or retraction of the deprecation primitive is itself a belief documenting the reversal.
Deprecation is distinct from retraction, which is reserved for beliefs that turned out false (per b029).
Confidence-field deprecation is the reference case for deprecation-as-pause: it may be reinstated in derived form if a concrete use-case ever materializes.
Enum-shaped fields on beliefs (kind, domain, artifact-scheme, others as introduced) take values from sets declared in dedicated contracts.

The constraint that a field's value is in a given enum is carried by the field's master contract (b038), while the enumeration of allowed values is carried by a dedicated enum contract per field (b039 for kind, b040 for artifact-scheme, b041 for domain); the two layers compose via deps.
Adding an enum value supersedes the enum contract for that field.

cb:b398.note: One definition: referent, URI form, role.

cb:b401.note: Describes the v1 stored contract field, contradicted by the b056 derived-grade rule; the right move is supersession or retirement in a follow-up adjudication, not decomposition.

cb:b403.note: Facets of one vocabulary entry, not conjoined assertions.

atoms: type:compound is a descriptive synthesis of facts from deps - the claim states what the deps together describe.
type:implication is a prescriptive derivation from deps - the claim states what must be done or must be true based on the deps.
A belief whose claim has both descriptive and prescriptive shapes is represented as two beliefs, one per type, linked via deps.

cb:b407.note: One fact plus illustration and standard citation.

atoms: `deps` is belief-to-belief logical derivation - the deps' claims together justify the current belief's claim - required on type:compound and type:implication, absent on type:primitive.
`subjects` is belief-to-entity topical reference - what the belief is about - including artifacts (files, threads, URLs), code modules, and sometimes other beliefs.
Aboutness and dependence are independent: a belief can be about another belief without depending on it, and can depend on another belief without being about it.

Logical underpinnings of code and data decisions trace through a three-layer chain: policy beliefs (kind:policy, type:primitive) state what must be true, contract beliefs (contract:true, type:implication) derive rules from policies via deps and express them in DSL (rules/invariants), and code modules implement the contract rules.
Each layer of the policy-contract-code chain links to the next: contracts dep on policies, and contracts cite their implementing code modules via subjects.
Discovery along the policy-contract-code chain is bidirectional via DAG traversal - no back-pointer field is needed because depended-on-by is computable from deps.

cb:b437.note: One vocabulary entry; contrast and examples are elaboration.

atoms: The audit chain for architectural decisions runs: code -> contract -> graph -> plan/recap metadata -> raw conversation.
The audit chain's bottom rung is currently ephemeral, single-machine, prunable transcript files.
Lossy synthesis is sufficient for most plans but may be inadequate for architecturally load-bearing decisions where the audit needs to reach the raw negotiation.
When (if ever) durable-in-version-control verbatim conversation is worth the storage and maintenance cost is an open question.
A codepath is a cb collection.

A codepath claim anchors to a within-file site via code:<repo-relative-path>#<anchor>, where everything after the first '#' is one opaque literal substring anchor with an optional trailing '@<N>' occurrence selector (a literal trailing '@<digits>' is percent-encoded as '%40<digits>').
Line numbers are never stored in code anchors; they resolve at render/run time.
A missing code anchor is a maintenance signal, and multiple matches render against the first match with a tighten-this-anchor warning.
Codepath ordering and branching live in an output-target render-spec (entry plus render_steps rows), never in the claim beliefs.

The cb-schema-v2 design (plans/cb-schema-v2/design.md, decided 2026-06-10) replaces the three-type schema with four structural types, one per epistemic operation: primitive (attest), compound (aggregate), inference (infer), directive (prescribe).
The v1 implication type conflated two moods: descriptive conclusions licensed to exceed their deps, and prescriptions the house stands behind.

The machinery already sorted by the hidden mood boundary: materialization, the conflict audit, and contract grading attach only to prescriptions, while staleness and supersession-on-evidence respond to falsification of descriptions.
Contract remains a structural grade in v2 - the machine-checkable grade of a directive.
The boundary between inference and directive is direction of fit made operational: ask what would count as the belief being wrong.
An inference is falsified - if the world disagrees, the belief is defective and is superseded or retracted (mind fits world).

A directive is violated - the world disobeys and the response is to flag the violation rather than revise the rule - or withdrawn - the house stops standing behind it, superseding it with a successor or retiring it (world fits mind).
The author-facing trichotomy: falsified means inference; violated means directive; withdrawn means directive.
In schema v2, type is a near-function of three checkable properties: type = f(mood(kind), grounding(artifact/deps), scope(subjects)).
Mood is bound by the kind-type derivation table contract.
Grounding separates the descriptive types: artifact with no deps means primitive; deps mean compound or inference.

Subject containment separates compound from inference - a compound's subjects must be a subset of the union of its deps' subjects, with empty subjects passing vacuously, while an inference is licensed to widen scope.
What stays judgment in v2 typing: choosing the kind, and the residual gray zone where a claim is subject-contained yet synthesizing; the write flow owns that residue.
The inference type is named for the ampliative move it records.
A deduction's conclusion is contained in its premises and can fail only when a premise fails; deductive consequences are infinite and free, so the graph never stores them.

An inference's conclusion outruns its deps - a generalization or an abduction - which is why it can be falsified while every dep stays true, and why the supersession-on-falsification lifecycle exists for it.

The compound is the one entailment the schema stores (conjunction introduction), with subject containment as its formal shadow; the epistemic work a compound records is the selection of what to assemble.

Type membership tracks the deps-to-claim relation, never the author's mental act, which is why the verifier interrogates scope rather than asking what kind of reasoning the author believes they performed.

A prescription is adopted, and adoption grounds in one of two places: in beliefs (deps - guidance resting on a verdict) or in a stipulation event (an artifact citing plan:, user:, or session: - a convention fixed by decision rather than derived from evidence).
Schema v2 requires of a non-contract directive deps or a stipulation artifact.
The deps-or-stipulation requirement legitimizes conventions as directives without manufacturing fake deps; contract-grade directives keep their existing empty-deps exemption.

The framework graph migrated to the four-type v2 schema on 2026-06-10: 76 nodes re-typed, the b026/b027/b029/b031/b032/b038 contract family superseded by b051-b056, new contracts b057/b058/b059, and the CLAUDE.md render beliefs superseded and regenerated.

All seven sibling collections (codepath, method, sdl, toy, lib, agent-behavior, paradigm) migrated to the v2 schema via mix cb.migrate.v2, with adjudicated splits sdl:a006 -> a008+a009 and toy:a9 -> a10+a11, the D3 trim sdl:a3 -> a010, and six agent-behavior mood re-homes (b396-b401).
All eight collections verify under v2; sdl reproduces exactly its two teaching method-check failures.
Framework canon changes only through its own write flow, including at the foundations.

The status-lifecycle contract was superseded via the lifecycle it defines (b029 -> b053), and the type enum was replaced through adjudication by a node typed in the values it introduces (b026 -> b051).
Because there is no maintenance hatch, the completeness of the audit trail is structural rather than behavioral - the history can be trusted without trusting that everyone behaved.

cb:b529.note: Inference; gradient plus necessary-condition qualifier is one conclusion.

atoms: Per-belief atomic files (one JSON file per node at beliefs/<ns>/<local>.json) are preferred over both the single-file array and per-entity grouping.
The cross-entity-composition concern recorded against per-entity files (cb:b112) does not apply to per-node files: every belief is addressed uniformly and composition stays via deps.
Per-node files eliminate the _keys whole-array churn-suppression workaround, align with the anti-digest principle (cb:b386), and prepare the store for a database backend.

Per-node storage constraint: multi-node writes (e.g. supersession) lose single-file write-atomicity and become N file writes, acceptable at local/single-writer scale or via an all-or-nothing write helper.
cb:b112's supersession is deferred to cb:b560 so the active graph does not claim per-file storage before the code implements it.
Schema rule in force: no `confidence` field.
Schema rule in force: no `patch` kind.
Schema rule in force: no separate `implication` prose field, since meaning is carried by `claim` plus `deps`.
Schema rule in force: attestations ground their claim with an `artifact` URI and dated `evidence`.
Schema rule in force: every active prescription grounds in deps or a stipulation artifact (per b059).
Schema rule in force: contract-grade is derived, not stored - a prescription with non-empty `rules`/`invariants` is contract-grade, with no `contract` field carried (per b056).

OKF bundle doc discovery (CB.Okf.Manifest.doc_paths/1, shared with the validator) enumerates markdown docs via Elixir's Path.wildcard, whose default match_dot: false skips dot-directories - so the beliefs/nursery/threads/.sessions/ draft area is structurally invisible to manifest build and validation.
The leading dot in .sessions is load-bearing: it is what keeps the frontmatter-less, per-turn-rewritten session drafts out of the validated bundle.
Passing match_dot: true to the OKF discovery wildcard, or renaming the .sessions directory without the dot, would silently pull the session drafts into discovery and break manifest validation.

cb:b569.claim: Nursery conventions: the nursery artifact is the proto-belief document - one per separable matter, mood carried only by the structural type system on its mint-manifest rows, lifecycle marked by the Proto-Belief: commit trailer.
invariants: The names focus, seed (for documents), brief, and plan are retired, and no informal genre register survives them; threads keep seed informally as the seed bed ideas germinate in
A plan is a proto-belief document whose mint-manifest rows are predominantly prescriptions
One proto-belief document per separable matter: separable means the strands' eventual mint-manifest rows stand on independent argument; strands whose rows need each other's reasoning share a document
Split and merge are cheap before the gate; the boundary only turns costly at mint
The commit trailer for document lifecycle events is Proto-Belief:, completing the chain Thread: -> Proto-Belief: -> Belief:

cb:b546.claim: Fold the knowledge standard (amieval/knowledge) into composable-beliefs as the okf: extension in a fresh execution session: move the standard into composable-beliefs/okf/, re-import the belief namespace knowledge: -> okf:, rewire couplings, reconcile the moved docs, handle dangling document: pointers with a light touch (leave historical or append corrective evidence, never rewrite), then decommission the knowledge repo - keeping the conceptual line as a namespace (cb: vs okf:), not a repo, with detailed steps and verification in plan:okf-fold.
cb:b546.note: The dropped inventory (related okf-collection beliefs, out-of-scope recommendations) lives in the plan:okf-fold artifact the claim cites; the previous claim is preserved in the migration evidence entry.

cb:b540.claim: A decision-weight session - one that mints or supersedes beliefs grounded in a user:/session: stipulation, settles a stance, or adjudicates contradictory positions - persists its thread verbatim at close, not only as the condensed transcript of cb:b520.
invariants: The verbatim thread (user messages and assistant prose as written, tool activity bracketed) lands in the repo the thread centers on, by subject: strategy/direction threads to the private direction repos, plan-scale dev threads to the co-located plans/<set>/ convention
Every belief minted that session is retro-paired (cb:b507) with a document: pointer to that thread
The directive remains the SSOT and must stay self-bootstrapping on its own claim and deps; the verbatim thread is provenance a reader may consult, never a dependency a fresh agent needs to act
Until the session-artifact pipeline (cb:b518) makes the real transcript resolvable, the verbatim thread is a faithful reconstruction and this convention is the bridge to that mechanization
A plan is optional scaffolding warranted only at plan-scale (cb:b496), authored in the repo whose system it concerns (cb:b492), never standing in for the directive it grounds

cb:b587.claim: History rewriting is prohibited wherever commits carry or will carry provenance - feature branches included, not only the default branch cb:b573 already protects: no rebase, no squash, no amend, no --reset-author on commits that exist - and tooling advice that contradicts this rule, specifically the git-check Stop hook's amend --reset-author or rebase --exec remedy for commits it flags as Unverified, is disregarded.
atoms: The graph's provenance machinery dereferences commit SHAs (commit: artifacts, Belief:/Proto-Belief:/Thread: trailers, mix cb.verify.commits), and a session's local commits become citation targets the moment a mint lands, so rewriting them severs the belief-commit loop before any repository setting can intervene.

The git-check Stop hook's Unverified flag is a false positive in this environment: commits are SSH-signed at creation by the environment's signing helper and verify on GitHub once pushed, but git reports %G? as N for SSH-signed commits when no gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile is configured, while committer identity is already correct.
The git-check Stop hook re-fires every turn until commits are pushed - expected and benign, never a reason to rewrite.

cb:b440.claim: In parent/child architectural dev work, the user does not delegate understanding to the agent: the user must stay on-the-loop at every depth of nested work, and a new depth level cannot arise without the user's participation in creating it.
atoms: Sub-agent delegation abstracts in-progress reasoning away from the user and forecloses intervention; parent/child structure, where the user stays on-the-loop at every depth, is distinguished from delegation by exactly this.

The on-the-loop requirement maps onto an operations/engineering mode split: in operational work delegation is fine (bounded, mechanical work), while in architectural work delegation breaks the user's ability to audit the reasoning that produces architectural decisions.

cb:b384.claim: Materialized implications require periodic drift audits to confirm their effects still hold; the audit is a first-class maintenance cycle, not a one-off.
invariants: A drift audit iterates over implications with non-null materialized field, re-evaluates whether the action's effects are still present, and either bumps materialized.last_verified to the audit date or emits a new primitive asserting the drift and proposing a re-materialization action
Audit cadence is case-dependent - some implications (module splits) decay slowly, others (bash removal) decay faster; default cadence TBD, initial proposal quarterly with per-implication overrides

cb:b382.claim: Plans encode intent, not implementation: intent lives in the DAG as beliefs, current state is assessed at execution time against the live codebase, and the implementation sequence is generated fresh when work is picked up, from intent plus current state.
invariants: A plan file survives only if it encodes sequencing that cannot be generated - actual choreography across sessions, or constraints not derivable from current state; everything else is a DAG assertion
atoms: Static implementation steps in plans are liabilities because the world drifts between plan authoring and plan execution.
Plans that restate what is generable at execution time duplicate the DAG and the codebase, the two stores that do not drift relative to themselves.

cb:b381.claim: When preflight surfaces a conflicting node against a proposed belief, the agent must not silently rework, weaken, or abandon the proposal to fit the existing node: the proposal enters adjudication per the consensus mechanism (human-as-judge, multi-agent patch, or tiered review), because retraction after evidence is valid but retraction under the perceived authority of existing DAG state without adjudication is sycophancy-toward-the-DAG and is disallowed; the rule also applies to user pushback, but DAG pushback is the foundational case.
atoms: Sycophancy-toward-the-DAG is distinct from social sycophancy (a051 reflexive agreement, a054 uncritical acceptance of user speculation): it defers to accumulated structure rather than to a person, and is invisible without an explicit rule naming it.

cb:b545.note: Decision memo in an action-item; likely overtaken by events - the commit: scheme it weighs now exists in cb:b067 and mix cb.verify.commits ships - so the right move is cb.todo.close with discharge notes, not decomposition.

cb:b564.note: Discrete worklist whose enumerable content is the work itself; closes via cb.todo.close.

cb:b541.note: Discrete feature todo; content is the work description.

cb:b580.claim: Commit autonomously; push only when explicitly instructed: a session commits its own completed work as it lands - including ride-along artifacts the repo's hooks stage, such as the .sessions transcript renders - without asking first, while the remote is the gate: pushing, merging, and anything else that publishes beyond the local clone requires explicit instruction.
atoms: The ask-before-commit rule deadlocked against the ride-along render lane: the Stop hook stages the session render each turn expecting it to ride along with the session's commits, and a policy that gates every commit on the operator turns that expectation into a per-turn interruption.

cb:b577.note: Discrete decision todo (archive shelf); options list is the work description.

cb:b573.claim: Merge-commit only: pull requests land on main via merge commits; squash merging and rebase merging are prohibited and disabled in repository settings (2026-07-02) - doubly held, since settings enforce it mechanically and this prescription records why, so the setting cannot later be flipped back as a harmless preference.
atoms: Squash and rebase merging rewrite merged history to new SHAs, while the graph's provenance machinery dereferences merged SHAs: commit: artifacts cite implementing commits by content address, Belief: trailers bind commits to nodes, and nodes like cb:b566 carry commit: citations whose targets must exist in every fresh clone.
A squash or rebase merge leaves cited SHAs reachable only through the host's hidden PR refs - absent from a clean clone - so mix cb.verify.commits fails and the belief-commit loop is severed.

cb:b568.claim: Atomic lifecycle commits: every commit recording an authoring-lifecycle transition records exactly one transition of one artifact - the belief atomicity doctrine transposed from nodes to commits - so a commit conjoining separable lifecycle events is a mis-authored bundle, split at commit time.
invariants: Atomic means one event, not one file: a brief together with the index and manifest updates it forces is one event
Typed trailers (Thread:, Focus:, Belief:) map one-to-one onto commits, so a trailer grep returns exactly one artifact's history

cb:b547.claim: A repo move (folding, renaming, or relocating) is not done until its inbound document:/code: artifacts resolve again: before decommissioning, sweep every dependent graph for the old path and repoint each typed artifact with a corrective evidence append (mix cb.evidence) to the new location, leaving the original entry as dated history (claims and detail prose are immutable and stay as written).
atoms: Folding, renaming, or relocating a repo orphans every inbound document:/code: artifact that other graphs cite into it: the artifact enum (cb:b066) has no rebind operation, so the pointers silently dangle the moment the path moves.

The okf-fold (cb:b546) is the worked example of repo-move orphaning: deleting amieval/knowledge left four cb: evidence artifacts (cb:b518/b540/b543/b544) pointing at document:../knowledge/..., caught only in the post-fold audit.

cb:b496.claim: Persistence ceremony is proportionate to stance: a position document earns its keep when the reasoning is the artifact - a stance whose verbatim wording matters - with its claims then extracted into the graph, while observations with an obvious prescription skip the document and go straight into the graph as directives, the gap carried as rationale prose or a small design-gap node underneath, stipulated by the thread that surfaced them.
atoms: If every wart became a three-artifact pipeline, the pipeline would stop being read.

cb:b463.claim: Belief ids are namespaced as `namespace:local-id` (e.g. `cb:b038`, `agent-behavior:a054`), with exactly one owning collection per namespace, so ids are globally unique.
invariants: Deps may cross namespaces and resolve globally, but `cb:` depends only within `cb:`; every other collection may depend on `cb:`
The id separator is `:`

cb:b439.claim: kind:policy on a belief signifies a mental/intentional commitment about how the system or agent should behave, held exactly while the commitment is not mechanically enforced - if a verifier checks it, a generator emits from it, or a hook fires on it today, it is a contract, schema rule, or definition instead.
invariants: kind:policy is mutually exclusive with contract-grade; policies carry prose claim only, no rules or invariants
Every kind:policy belief carries a non-empty name field for stable citation

When a policy's intent is later mechanized, the policy migrates: a contract is authored citing the policy via deps per b409's three-layer chain, and the policy either remains (stating the intent the contract enforces) or is superseded by a new policy stating the post-mechanization intent
cb:b439.note: The original's 'mutually exclusive with contract:true' modernized to contract-grade per b056 (the stored field no longer exists).

cb:b406.claim: A belief's claim describes the optimal state in present tense: it states what is true, not what was changed or what is being avoided.
invariants: Transitional language (renamed, previously, no longer, remain), enumeration of negations (X is not Y, X does not carry Z), and reactionary framing belong in evidence entries with dates
atoms: A claim survives once context fades; framing that depends on prior state goes stale and misleads.

cb:b375.claim: Principles that should influence future decisions persist as DAG beliefs; concrete sequenced action lists persist as plan documents - the distinguishing question is whether the content advises future decisions (DAG) or sequences present steps (plan).
atoms: A single initiative often produces both a DAG principle and a plan executing it once.

cb:b120.claim: Beliefs and contracts are two roles sharing one store: a belief says 'this is true'; a contract says 'this will remain true.'
invariants: Ordinary beliefs become stale and get superseded; contracts are behavioral invariants that get violated or upheld, not superseded
